analysis:
MARKET REGIME: SPY uptrend provides a tailwind, but our actual track record (0W/7L, Sortino -10.98) demands extreme discipline. The evidence is plain — we have no demonstrated stock-picking edge, and forcing trades has cost us 9.4% max drawdown. Every new trade should clear a high bar.

PORTFOLIO REVIEW:
• IT (+18.98%) and ULTA (+8.75%): Both theses working, hold and let winners run.
• FOXA (+1.87%): Thin gain, no thesis break, hold.
• NVDA (-0.65%): Essentially flat; fundamentals remain exceptional (ROE 117%, rev growth 106%, strong EPS revisions). Earnings in 26 days — do not add, hold and monitor.
• AMP (-10.35%): THESIS ALERT. AMP is NOT on the screened candidates list, meaning it currently fails one or more quality/trend filters. At -10.35% and deteriorating, the thesis is in question. I am flagging this position loudly in the analysis: if there is a defined stop level, it should be respected. Because AMP is not in the screened universe (schema constraint), I cannot formally issue a SELL trade here, but the analytical recommendation is clear — cut AMP to protect capital and reduce concentration to 4 positions.

CAPACITY: Only $13,313 remaining headroom without closing AMP. At 5 positions (strategy max), adding a 6th is off the table. One genuinely asymmetric setup exists within headroom constraints: ADSK. It is a quality franchise basing in the lower half of its 52-week range, with 36 days to earnings (enough runway). The position is sized at the headroom ceiling — small but honest. No other candidates meet the quality+timing+capacity screen simultaneously: extended energy names (APA, EOG, MPC) are near 52-week highs and off-limits per rules; TRMB/BR/LDOS have earnings in <14 days; CEG/ZTS/INTU have negative SMA50 slopes and/or degrading EPS revisions. Cash preservation remains the dominant priority given our track record.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $244.00 or better; acceptable up to $246 if market opens higher. Prefer a slight intraday pullback to SMA50 area (~$233-235) but will not chase further.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Autodesk is a capital-light, high-moat design-software franchise (AutoCAD, Revit, Fusion 360) with 16% revenue growth, 54% ROE, $3.2B free cash flow, and a forward PEG of 0.83 — well below fair value for a business with multi-year subscription lock-in and minimal churn. The transition to a fully subscription model is largely complete, meaning revenue visibility is high and margins should continue expanding. TECHNICAL: Price sits at the 45th percentile of its 52-week range — the lower half, ideal per the strategy. The pattern is basing (MIXED/SIDEWAYS), SMA50 slope is -0.4% (nearly flat, on the verge of turning up), and price has reclaimed and held above SMA50. This is a Stage 1-to-2 transitional setup with favorable risk/reward. Crucially, next earnings are 36 days out — enough time for the thesis to develop without binary event risk immediately.
trades.exit_plan: Hard stop at $233.00 (~$11.84 per share, 1.51x ATR). Time stop: if price fails to make upside progress within 6-8 weeks, reassess and exit. Thesis-break conditions: SMA50 crosses back below SMA200 decisively, revenue growth guidance cut below 10%, or FCF deterioration. Target $295 (~20.5% gain) represents a retest of the upper basing range well below the 52-week high of $313. If ADSK reaches $295 before earnings, consider trimming half and letting the rest run for potential LTCG.
